iOS 26.6、iPadOS 26.6 and related software updates have rolled out, and Apple has detailed the extensive security patches included in today's new system versions.

The Apple security updates in iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 affect iPhones and iPads in multiple ways.

In iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, Apple disclosed over 75 security patches for iPhone and iPad, covering several areas of the system.

More specifically, Apple's security advisory lists 78 distinct vulnerability entries, involving 87 separate CVE identifiers. Because some entries involve more than one CVE, the number of CVEs is higher.

Apple has not indicated that any of the vulnerabilities patched in iOS 26.6 were actively exploited in the wild.

Among Apple's lengthy list, the following patches are particularly worth noting:

  • A vulnerability in MediaRemote could allow an app to gain root privileges.
  • A vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder could allow an app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges.
  • Vulnerabilities in Game Center and libc could allow a malicious app to escape its sandbox.
  • A vulnerability in CloudAttestation could allow a malicious app to bypass code signing requirements.
  • A vulnerability in ImageIO could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image.
  • Three vulnerabilities in SceneKit could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing maliciously crafted files.
  • An Accessibility issue could leak sensitive data via iPhone Mirroring to someone with physical access to the device.
  • A vulnerability in Contacts could allow an app to add contacts without user authorization.

Kernel, WebKit and Wi-Fi patches

Apple also patched more than a dozen kernel vulnerabilities, with potential impacts including corrupting or writing kernel memory, leaking kernel memory, bypassing network filtering, and causing unexpected system termination.

WebKit also received a large number of patches, with related vulnerabilities potentially leaking process memory, leaking whether a user has visited a particular link, causing interface spoofing, violating iframe sandbox rules, allowing apps to read files outside the sandbox, or causing Safari to crash.

An additional Wi-Fi vulnerability could allow a nearby attacker to corrupt process memory.

After the 78 documented security patches, Apple included a separate "Additional recognition" section with 12 acknowledgements.

These entries are intended to thank researchers for their assistance and are not presented as standalone security patches, nor assigned additional CVE identifiers.

The complete list of patches and researcher acknowledgements is available on Apple's website.

Security patches for Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro

Apple's newly released macOS Tahoe 26.6 security advisory lists 155 distinct CVEs.

In addition to a number of patches shared with iPhone and iPad, the Mac update also addresses vulnerabilities that could be used to allow an app to gain root privileges, escape the sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper checks or privacy preferences, and access protected data.

Apple also released security updates for older versions of macOS today, but those updates are not counted in the figures above.

Apple also detailed the patches in watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6, and visionOS 26.6. After removing overlapping items across platforms, Apple's latest updates collectively address 194 distinct CVEs.

Apple previously stated that, due to AI-powered attack tools, several security patches were released early in last month's iOS 26.5.2 update.
